And they drew close, and they drew close to Rabbainu, yes.

And they supported him and.. yes, oy.

They did not—the first time in their lives, the three, these are the three wise men—

They, they saw such a commotion for the first time in their lives. So when they heard, they asked:

“What is this commotion? What? What is there?”

“Ho, have you not heard that Yisroel Ber became Breslov?”

“We heard. Nu, what is there? Nu.”

“Nu, what is there? They took him, Rav Tzvi.”

And they told him.

They saw such a commotion:

“Yisroel Ber became Breslov, and Rav Tzvi went to pray..”

On Sunday I was afraid: perhaps the mukhtar wants money?

He will come again and take me to prison—money.

“Where is Rav Tzvi?”

Money, only money, money.

So, so, so I saw a place near the Karlin synagogue.

A place, a closed place, a place where one cannot be seen. I was there all day near the synagogue, yes.

Perhaps Mordechai will come with the policemen; I.. and they..

No one knew who, where, where I was, so he could search.

In any case I, I was there until Minchah.

At Minchah I went up to the synagogue from the place where I was, to the synagogue,

to pray Minchah, to hear Kedushah and.. there came, there came the elder Rav Kehas.

Rav Kehas, he, he was a Karliner, and also, and also the father of the woman of, the wife of Rav Tzvi Rosenthal was also a Karliner, and they were friends.

So Rav Kehas went to pray Minchah and heard that the police had taken Mordechai, the mukhtar, to Istanbul, and that there was a serious complaint against him that he was a spy, that he.. yes.

So Rav Kehas said:

“This is Rebbe Yisroel, Rebbe Yisroel; this is the doing of Rebbe Yisroel.

Rebbe Yisroel punished him; he, he gave him a punishment. Hashem gave him a punishment for this, for this Shabbos.” He—they took him, and from then on he vanished. I did not see him, {...}. Teveria did not see him anymore. Perhaps he.. I think they put him to death. A spy—there was a complaint that he was a spy.

segments.en:
Then the English, they, they, they, they were at war with Turkey.

And here it was Turkey; Syria too was Turkey and Lebanon was Turkey—everything was Turkey, yes.

{...}

Nu, Turkey, and the complaint was that Rav Mordechai was a spy; he, he, he was a spy.

Everything that there was here in Turkey, he passed on to the enemy, to their enemy, so that was already espionage.

So he did not return alive; from the day, from that Sunday, he did not return to Teveria, nor to the Land of Yisroel.

No, they do not know where, where he is, where he is, yes.

Whether they put him to death and.. in any case, they do not know.

Teveria remained without the mukhtar, without Mordechai, yes.

He made such a Shabbos, so he had such a Sunday: they took him to Istanbul and he did not return alive.

It was like such a spectacle; the whole city was in an uproar.

The Sephardim, they, they are a people unto themselves; they do not know what there is among the Ashkenazim.

And the Ashkenazim do not know what there is among the Sephardim.

Two, two, two separate faiths: these are Sephardim and these are Ashkenazim, yes. One of them does not resemble the other. But the affair of Rav Tzvi—the entire Sephardic community, the whole city, all the Sephardim—

knew that it happened, that such a thing happened:

that Rav Tzvi went to pray, to pray on Friday, and did not, did not return.

Nu, the whole city, both the Ashkenazim and the Sephardim, everyone was, was in such an uproar:

How does one take..? How does one do such a thing? On Friday one goes to pray and does not..?

This, this is not, this, this is such a wondrous affair as we have not yet heard.

The affair—how is it possible...? How does one do such a thing?”

He walked to Yerushalayim on foot on Friday; he had no money to travel.

He walked on Friday, went to pray, and from the synagogue walked to Yerushalayim, yes.
